raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation For PD transfer on NPU, adopt Mooncake as the backend by reusing the existing community code logic. ## Modifications Based on it, we merged the MF logic into Mooncake to support MF transfers, enabling SGLang to directly use Mooncake's transfer backend. ## Accuracy Tests deepseek-v4-flash A5 ## Speed Tests and Profiling deepseek-v4-flash A5 The result is comparable to using MF directly. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #40082444276](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40082444276) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #40082444368](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40082444368) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #40082444330](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40082444330)

Hi @Liwansi, as the maintainer of the elastic EP module, this PR has the risk of breaking the functionalities of elastic EP, as Mooncake PG requires a shared TE instance to be initialized before `_init_parallel_groups`. Although there are workarounds, if this PR is merged as is, it may impact the development of current elastic EP features.

Happy to discuss and work on a path that is safe and sound. Thanks!

> Hi @Liwansi, as the maintainer of the elastic EP module, this PR has the risk of breaking the functionalities of elastic EP, as Mooncake PG requires a shared TE instance to be initialized before `_init_parallel_groups`. Although there are workarounds, if this PR is merged as is, it may impact the development of current elastic EP features.
> 
> Happy to discuss and work on a path that is safe and sound. Thanks!

i see. the thing is we need to init ccl before init te, in order to get a drv singleton handle for ccl first. **BUT** this is just under certain networking topology which is not commonly seen on the latest hardware generations. we will try to see first if we can do workarounds underneath, will let you know if we have any

> > Hi @Liwansi, as the maintainer of the elastic EP module, this PR has the risk of breaking the functionalities of elastic EP, as Mooncake PG requires a shared TE instance to be initialized before `_init_parallel_groups`. Although there are workarounds, if this PR is merged as is, it may impact the development of current elastic EP features.
> > Happy to discuss and work on a path that is safe and sound. Thanks!
> 
> i see. the thing is we need to init ccl before init te, in order to get a drv singleton handle for ccl first. **BUT** this is just under certain networking topology which is not commonly seen on the latest hardware generations. we will try to see first if we can do workarounds underneath, will let you know if we have any

well, it's quite tough to do workarounds. however, we will keep the code as-is for now and this pr will be closed. for any users require that networking topology, we will guide them to use `ascend` transfer backend instead. thx for the help @UNIDY2002
